obligation: HIPAA breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual by first-class mail (or email if the individual agreed)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member or agent (164.404(a)(2))

obligation: HIPAA substitute notice
trigger: Insufficient or out-of-date contact information (common for 911 patients and callers)
deadline: With the individual notices
notify: Fewer than 10: alternative written notice, phone, or other means. 10 or more: conspicuous website posting for 90 days or major print or broadcast media, with a toll-free number active for 90 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if contact information is missing

obligation: HIPAA notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (and no later than 60 days after discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: Breach affecting fewer than 500 individuals
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal

obligation: HIPAA media notice
trigger: Breach involving more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving each state or jurisdiction where more than 500 residents are affected
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - count per state (FL, GA, AL, SC, TN, and any other state)
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with the Vice President, Corporate Communications

obligation: HIPAA law enforcement delay
trigger: Law enforcement states that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: For the period in a written statement; up to 30 days from an oral statement, which must be documented
notify: Hold the affected notices; document the request

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A business associate (CAD vendor, ePCR vendor, revenue cycle vendor, telephony vendor) discovers a breach of the company's PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after the BA's discovery (company BAAs require 10 days)
notify: The company's Chief Privacy Officer

obligation: Company as business associate: notice to SL-1 public EMS agencies (outbound)
trigger: Breach of an agency's PHI in the billing services environment
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery (SL-1 BAAs commit to 10 days)
notify: Each affected agency (covered entity), with the identity of each affected individual and available facts
owner: Vice President, EMS Billing Services with the Chief Privacy Officer

obligation: Company as business associate: notice to SL-2 Medicaid programs and plans (outbound)
trigger: Breach of members' PHI in the managed transportation platform
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery (SL-2 BAAs commit to shorter contract terms; check each)
notify: Each affected state Medicaid program and managed care plan, with the identity of each affected member
owner: President, Managed Transportation with the Chief Privacy Officer

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (definitions, including whether medical information is covered, vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days; some allow HIPAA-compliant notice to satisfy the state duty
notify: Affected residents of each state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; counsel's state matrix
clock_starts: Varies by state (often determination of a breach)
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with outside counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company
trigger: Vendor that maintains personal information has a breach
deadline: Varies by state
notify: The company

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information (includes medical and health insurance information) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (law enforcement delay under 501.171(4)(b))
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida deemed compliance through HIPAA notice (worked example)
trigger: Notice given under the rules of the primary or functional federal regulator (HHS for HIPAA)
deadline: The HIPAA notice counts if a copy is timely provided to the Department of Legal Affairs
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (copy of the HIPAA notice)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, content of notices)

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if that determination is made (HIPAA duties still apply separately)

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors and network providers holding Florida residents' personal information

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material, including an operational outage with no data loss
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.4)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines (the company may ask; it cannot decide)

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, incident responders with knowledge, and executives (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: County PSAP notice of manual dispatch
trigger: Dispatch moves to manual mode, or a CAD-to-CAD interface fails, for any county
deadline: Immediately by phone or radio to the PSAP supervisor
notify: Each affected county PSAP supervisor

obligation: County contract manager written notice
trigger: Service disruption affecting a county's 911 response
deadline: Per each agreement (standard term: verbal within 1 hour and written within 24 hours; check each agreement)
notify: County EMS contract managers
owner: Vice President, Government Relations and County Contracts

obligation: SL-1 agency notice of service disruption
trigger: Incident affecting billing services or agency data
deadline: Per client agreement (standard term: 24 hours for a service outage; 10 days for a breach)
notify: 46 public EMS agencies

obligation: SL-2 Medicaid program and plan notice
citation: State Medicaid broker contracts and plan agreements (contract)
trigger: Incident affecting trip scheduling, member data, or encounter reporting
deadline: Per contract (check each; several require notice of a security incident within 24 hours)
notify: 3 state Medicaid programs and 6 managed care plans

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As early as practical (supports OFAC mitigation and investigation)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until it takes effect. As proposed, the company would be covered (above the SBA size standard in a critical infrastructure sector; EMS to a population of 50,000 or more)

obligation: CJIS incident reporting (IR-6)
trigger: Incident involving criminal justice information
deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Organizational incident handlers; CSO, SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official; FBI CJIS ISO
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company does not access criminal justice information (P03 section 1). Would apply only if a CJI feed were ever connected

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule
trigger: Breach of PHR identifiable health information by a non-HIPAA vendor
deadline: Within 60 days after discovery
notify: Individuals, FTC, media
applies_at_this_tier: No - covered entity and business associate acting as such (318.1)

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging vendors
notify: Carrier

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or subcontracts identified; recheck if one is signed

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or subcontracts identified; recheck if one is signed
